Resolution hinges on the official 24-hour maximum recorded at the Incheon station, with minimal model spread currently supporting the narrow 34–36°C window.

eventMetadata.context_description: Traders price 32–33°C as the clear favorites for Tokyo’s August 7 maximum because Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and ensemble models show the Kanto region under persistent subtropical high pressure, with daytime heating expected to reach the low-to-mid 30s amid typical early-August insolation and light winds. The narrow 2-percentage-point spread between the leaders reflects model uncertainty over minor variables such as afternoon cloud cover, boundary-layer mixing, and the precise strength of the urban heat-island effect, which can add 1–2 °C in central districts. Seasonal outlooks note temperatures running near or slightly above the 31.8 °C climatological normal, yet no strong signal supports either a notable cool surge or extreme heat that would shift probabilities toward 31 °C or 34 °C. Updated model runs and JMA briefings through the evening of August 6 remain the key near-term catalysts.
